name: WARP-8
author: David Ryan
description: WARP-8 turns the M-VAVE FM-1 into a pocket drum machine: LOOM-8's sequencer, mixer and effects with every track a drum kit. Eight kits of eleven keys each play 73 drum models, 43 of them Hortator's (the 808 and 909 family, Plaits' drums, a struck membrane, FM, and the voices measured from the Machinedrum), each key with its own envelope, filter and sends, and 143 of Hortator's factory sounds a turn away. A sample player, a break slicer and MIDI out tracks remain. A fork of LOOM-8 by Charles Vestal.
credits: A fork of LOOM-8 by Charles Vestal (MPL-2.0; github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-loom). Built on fm1-base and felucca-bsp, from Felucca by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments). Supersaw (brocade): after NuSaw (MIT). Cane, voile and gingham: Mutable Instruments Braids by Emilie Gillet (MIT). Acid: X0X's 303, from Open303 by Robin Schmidt (MIT), with jc303's Devilfish ranges by midilab and dm-Rat's RAT drive by Dave Mollen (GPL-3.0). Reverb: the plate after 9W9 by athousanddetails (with permission), the PlayStation modes PSXVerb (MIT). The 909 kick, snare and clap: renders of 9W9 by athousanddetails (with permission); the 909 models: 9W9's circuits (GPL-3.0); the hat and the 909 cymbals: ER-99's samples by Matthew Cieplak, through 9W9 (GPL-3.0). Hortator's drum models by DEADACTIVE, on Felucca, with ports of Mutable Instruments Plaits and DaisySP (GPL-3.0; the ports MIT). The x drums: after MACHINEDRUM by Omodaka9375 (MIT); sophie: Sophie by Matt Estela (MIT); clang: digisophie (MIT). USB MIDI host: Melodee's, by Adrien Tibi and Kerem Kilic (MPL-2.0). Bluetooth: Optimist's stack by Henri David (MPL-2.0), with Android's SBC encoder (Apache-2.0), micro-ecc by Kenneth MacKay (BSD-2-Clause) and the radio's set-up after JieLi's AC79 SDK (Apache-2.0). Fonts: Barlow, Terminus (SIL OFL 1.1).
